contact_model: Rigid contacts by default via PhysX 5 (SDF collisions, Featherstone articulation solver, Sec. 2.2); `Factory` assembly envs specifically use 'SDF-based contact generation, a contact reduction technique, and a Gauss-Seidel solver' (Sec. 6.4). ContactSensor exposes net normal force per body, optional filtered pairs, contact duration, average contact point, and a short history (Sec. 3.3.1); no contact-quality/penetration metric is defined (survey note).
solver: NVIDIA PhysX 5's internal rigid-body/Featherstone-articulation solver, used as-is; Factory assembly envs specifically named as using a Gauss-Seidel solver with SDF-based contact generation and contact reduction (Sec. 6.4). No timestep, decimation, or solver-iteration values are stated anywhere in the paper for the general (dexterous) suite; the only note is qualitative, that the Digit humanoid 'requires a higher solver iteration count for stable simulation' (Fig. 14).
throughput: DextrAH teacher task (state-based grasp-and-lift): over 900,000 FPS training throughput with 8 GPUs (RTX Pro 6000, the paper's only multi-GPU platform) and 16,384 environments (Sec. 4.1.1); Franka cabinet drawer task: over 1.6 million FPS at the same 8-GPU/16,384-environment setting. Single-GPU dexterous-suite numbers are not stated.
